commitResults.messageBody:
handleCommand had grown to roughly 60 lines and broke several of the
readability guidelines from the CS2103T code-quality reference at once:

- Long method: one method carried the dispatch logic and the full
  implementation of all nine command types, well past the ~30-line
  rule of thumb.
- Deep nesting: method -> try -> switch -> case block -> if -> throw
  pushed the core action of each command four to five levels deep.
- Single Level of Abstraction: high-level dispatch ("which command is
  this?") sat next to low-level mechanics (regex matching,
  Matcher.group() extraction, per-format exception construction).
- Duplication: the "match against PATTERN, throw a specific
  *FormatException on mismatch, then read the capture groups" block was
  copy-pasted four times (find, todo, deadline, event).
- Buried happy path: the actual work of each command was hard to pick
  out from its validation.

Changes:

- Extract one intention-revealing private method per command
  (handleList, handleFind, handleMark, handleUnmark, handleTodo,
  handleDeadline, handleEvent, handleDelete). handleCommand is now a
  flat dispatch table that reads top to bottom at a glance, and each
  handler is a two- to three-line method at a single level of
  abstraction.
- Add a requireMatch(pattern, command, exceptionSupplier) helper that
  captures the shared "match or fail" step once, removing the four-way
  duplication. The exception is passed as a Supplier so it is built
  only on the failure path, not on every command.
- Convert the dispatch to an arrow switch, matching the style already
  used in parseTask. This drops the break statements and the
  fall-through risk the guidelines call out under "avoid unsafe
  shortcuts", while the default branch still rejects unknown commands.

Behaviour is unchanged: every branch produces the same output and the
same exceptions as before, and bye is still intercepted upstream in
Hu9o before it can reach here. Verified with the unit suite, checkstyle,
and all six console UI test cases (output byte-identical).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace accumulator loops with stream pipelines
commitResults.messageBody:
Three loops in the persistence and search code were doing the classic
"walk a collection and accumulate into something" shape that a stream
states more directly. Converting them removes the mutable accumulator
and puts the intent (filter / transform / join) up front, in line with
the "make code obvious" readability guidance in the CS2103T code-quality
reference.

TaskList.findTasks:
- Was: allocate an empty TaskList, for-loop with an if that copies
  matching tasks into it, return it.
- Now: stream().filter(...).collect(toCollection(TaskList::new)).
  toCollection, rather than toList, preserves the TaskList return type
  so callers keep the task-aware operations.

Storage.dumpTasks:
- Was: a StringBuilder appended to inside a for-loop.
- Now: tasks.stream().map(task -> record + "\n").collect(joining()).
  The trailing newline per record is kept (so an empty list still
  produces an empty file) and the on-disk format is byte-for-byte
  unchanged. Appending to an external StringBuilder from forEach would
  have been a side-effecting stream, the very anti-pattern to avoid;
  joining() is the operation that matches "combine the pieces".

Storage.loadTasks:
- Already consumed the Stream<String> from Files.lines, but through a
  forEach whose body held an assignment and a null check.
- Now: lines.map(parser::parseTask).filter(Objects::nonNull)
  .forEach(tasks::addTask). The assignment becomes map, the null guard
  becomes filter, and forEach is left with one job. The IOException from
  Files.lines still needs an ordinary try/catch: checked exceptions do
  not compose with stream pipelines.

The read-eval-print loop in Hu9o.run was considered and deliberately
left as a while-loop: its exit command must also trigger a save, and it
performs a side effect per line, so a stream would only obscure it.

Behaviour verified unchanged: unit suite, checkstyle, and all six
console UI test cases pass, including the case that compares the saved
data file byte-for-byte.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Contacts page button, progress bar, typing indicator, and clear command
commitResults.messageBody:
Gives the GUI a top-right toggle to a Contacts page (Hu9o.getContactSummaries()
backs it), a `progress` command that renders a text progress bar of marked vs.
total tasks (Task.isDone()/TaskList.countDone()), an animated typing indicator
shown while a reply is prepared, and a GUI-only `clear` command that empties the
chat display without touching saved data. Updates the console UI test plan for
the new `progress` command and the widened unknown-command message.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Replies to greetings (hi/hello/hey/...) with a friendly line instead of an
unknown-command error, tailors the GUI welcome message to how many tasks are
loaded (empty / normal / "that's a lot"), and rewords every Hu9oException's
message to read like Hu9o talking rather than a terse validation error, while
keeping the exact wording every existing test/ui-test-plan.md case and
Hu9oTest substring check relies on. Adds a greeting-command UI test case and
updates the four cases whose expected output printed an error message.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for clear, progress, and the Contacts page
commitResults.messageBody:
Covers the three A-BetterGUI additions at the same logic level the existing
suite already uses (Hu9o.getResponse(...)/getContactSummaries() for
integration behaviour, direct Ui/TaskList construction for pure rendering
logic), rather than introducing a JavaFX UI-automation framework:
- Hu9o.isClearCommand(...): casing/spacing and false-positive cases.
- TaskList.countDone() and Ui.showProgress(...): empty, partial, and fully
  marked lists. The progress-bar tests go in UiTest (direct Ui/TaskList
  construction) rather than through Hu9o.getResponse(...), since
  Hu9o.createForGui() loads the real data/taskData.txt and would make the
  "empty list" case depend on whatever tasks happen to be saved on disk.
- Hu9o.getContactSummaries(): empty network, multiple people in order, and
  that reading it doesn't consume the error-flag state of a prior command.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Auto-create missing save files on load instead of only on save
commitResults.messageBody:
Saving already created data/ and the save file if missing (Files.createDirectories
before writing), but loading only skipped silently when a file wasn't found,
so the file only appeared on disk after the first save. Storage.loadTasks and
ContactStorage's loadPeople/loadLinks now create an empty file (and data/ if
needed) as soon as a missing one is detected, so taskData.txt, contactData.txt,
and contactLinks.txt always exist right after startup -- addressing the
recurring "file cannot be located" issue directly at load time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Add tests for clear, progress, and the Contacts page

commitResults.messageTitle: Add console UI test for auto-created save files on load
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage/ContactStorage's relative data-file paths resolve against the JVM's
real process working directory, which java.nio.file can't be redirected to
a @TempDir from within a plain JUnit test -- the same reason this project
had no prior Storage/ContactStorage tests. Verifies createEmptyFile the same
way this project already verifies save behaviour (dump-tasks-on-exit): run
the real jar in an isolated, data-less directory and inspect the resulting
files, rather than through a JUnit test. Input is empty so the process
crashes on EOF right after loading and before it could ever reach a save,
isolating the load-time fix from the pre-existing save-time behaviour.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Auto-create missing save files on load
